questions.q: Give an account of the living folk and tribal art traditions of India.
answer: Alongside its classical art, India has a wealth of living folk and tribal traditions, practised by communities in their daily and ritual life and passed down through generations.

answer.text: Among the best known is Madhubani, or Mithila, painting from Bihar, done by women with bright colours to depict gods, nature and weddings. Warli painting of Maharashtra is a tribal art using simple white geometric figures on mud walls to show community life. Pattachitra scrolls of Odisha and Bengal, Kalamkari cloth of Andhra Pradesh, and Phad scrolls of Rajasthan are other rich traditions.
Living crafts also include floor decorations such as rangoli and kolam, pottery and terracotta, textiles, and tribal metal casting like Dhokra.
These arts preserve cultural identity and oral heritage, and some, like Madhubani and Warli, have won global fame and Geographical Indication tags.

answer: Thus India's living traditions keep its folk creativity vibrant and rooted in community life.
